claims.text: Resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in HEAs is governed by the ability to form a refined microstructure containing hard secondary phases together with a stable passive film.
Selective additions such as Mo, B, or Si refine the HEA grain structure.
Selective alloying additions promote dispersed hard secondary phases such as sigma or TiB2.
B addition to an AlCoCrFeNiMo-based alloy refines the BCC phase and promotes in situ TiB2 formation.
Selective alloying additions produce a dense, low-defect passive film.
A low B addition enhances passive-film stability and corrosion resistance in an AlCoCrFeNiMoTiBx coating.
Hard secondary phases act as physical barriers to wear-induced damage and mechanical abrasion.
The refined microstructure impedes crack initiation.
A stable, uniform passive film resists chloride-induced pitting and corrosion.
The unmodified baseline HEA has a coarser microstructure than the selectively alloyed material.
The unmodified baseline HEA has a less uniform, more defect-prone passive film.
Under simultaneous wear-corrosion, the modified HEA will have a lower wear rate than the baseline.
Under simultaneous wear-corrosion, the modified HEA will have a lower corrosion current density than the baseline.
Combined degradation of the modified alloy will be less than the sum of its separately measured wear-only and corrosion-only degradation.
The proposed protection holds when mechanical loads are moderate enough to preserve passive-film integrity.
The proposed protection may fail under stresses that fracture the passive film or under chemical conditions that do not favor passivation.
The optimum addition levels, required grain refinement, and optimum passive-film composition and thickness are not yet defined.
A controlled baseline-versus-modified comparison in 3.5 wt% NaCl, with wear, electrochemical, microstructural, and surface analyses, can test the proposed mediator and outcomes.

The hypothesis is falsified if the modified alloy lacks statistically significant improvements in both wear and corrosion, combined degradation equals or exceeds the additive prediction, and the proposed refined microstructure and stabilized film are absent.
